answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by forcing each identity to forge a bond: it must lock real collateral before it can trade or vote. The bond is per identity and slashed on fraud, so an attacker wanting k fake voices must post k separate stakes, multiplying cost linearly. Honest agents publish their bonds and cover them with a velvet layer of peer-audited reputation that newcomers cannot borrow. A fake account hidden on a dune of anonymity inherits no trust from the crowd. Sybil stops being free speech and becomes an expensive purchase, with the attacker paying for every extra name.
